description: The tree willow of the foothill creeks: 6-15 m tall, with one or a few dark, furrowed trunks, reddish-brown to yellow twigs and long, narrow, finely toothed leaves shiny green above and whitish beneath. It stands on the banks and the first bench above the water along the larger creeks and rivers, its trunks often leaning out over the channel.

season_notes.winter: Bare dark trunks with a haze of reddish and yellow-brown twigs over the creek.
season_notes.spring: Catkins open with the new leaves in March and April; by May the cottony seed drifts on the water.
season_notes.summer: A rounded, rather open crown of glossy leaves that flash white underneath in the wind.
season_notes.fall: Leaves turn yellow and drop through November.

riparian.water: Needs a water table within reach of its roots all summer: the banks and first bench of creeks that run at least most of the year, and pond shores.

A mature streamside tree with a rounded, somewhat open crown about as wide as tall, a short clear trunk; colour is the linear r/g and b/g of the file's summer and fall leaf colours. notes: Red willow is the tallest native willow of the Sierra foothills and the Central Valley: a real tree 6-15 m (rarely 20), here 6-13 m in the file, on the banks and first floodplain bench of the larger creeks and rivers below about 1,300 m, with arroyo willow lower on the bank and cottonwood and sycamore behind it. Unlike the clumping arroyo and sandbar willows it usually has one to three trunks (stems [1, 3], stem_spread 18), decurrent: the trunk forks low into a few heavy, often leaning limbs (trunk.length_ratio 0.5, split_prob 0.45, lean up to 14 degrees, old trees to 24 as they tip toward the water). dbh 0.3-0.5 m on a 10 m tree: radius_ratio 0.035. Crown broad and rounded but open, wider in old trees (envelope widest 0.53 of height at mid-crown). Bark dark grey-brown, rough and deeply furrowed in old trees (bark_pattern furrowed). Twigs reddish-brown to yellow, shiny and brittle, the colour that gives the name: twig_rgb and the winter tint carry that red-brown so the bare crown reads warm. Leaves 6-17 cm, lanceolate with a long point, finely toothed, glossy green above and strongly glaucous (whitish) beneath, on short stalks: leaf_shape lanceolate, leaf_size_m 0.11, and a quarter of the palette lightened for the pale undersides that flash in wind. Catkins open with the leaves in March-April (not before them, as in arroyo willow), so no foliage.catkins on the bare winter texture. Yellow in fall, bare December-February (leaf_on_by_month). No snag: an old willow falls or splits and resprouts rather than standing dead; the old class carries the dead limbs. Architectural model provisional.
